gen-gf-baumans-gf-martel: Commanding tubes of letter up top, never swelling or thinning. Martel follows in a classic serif with moderate contrast and open apertures, and it wants a generous size so those openings can breathe.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-mate-sc: Mate SC reads like a text serif with a faint nib pressure in its round letters, dignified without stiffness. And Baumans above it keeps one flat line weight, so a long stretch of body feels softly pressed against a rigid heading.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-nanum-myeongjo: Nanum Myeongjo reads quietly, its curve tips stopping short of touching and its strokes barely modulated. Baumans is the one for making a statement with zero stroke contrast, while Nanum Myeongjo is the one for settling into refined, editorial text.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-noto-serif-hk: Baumans draws a round bowl whose outline never swells or thins, like a wrench-wide c cut from pipe. It is built for impact, while Noto Serif HK is built for dignified, editorial reading.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-noto-serif-jp: Baumans bends tubular strokes like copper pipe, each letter drawn at a single thickness. That is its talent; Noto Serif JP's talent is a literary, restrained thick-thin line.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-noto-serif-kr: Baumans forms each glyph from a ribbon of constant width, which gives headings a distinctive, commanding stamp. But Noto Serif KR does the opposite job well, using mild thick-thin differences and wide s curves to smooth out reading.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-noto-serif-sc: One stroke width runs through every letter of Baumans, and that single-minded line is what you notice first. Yet Noto Serif SC softens things with a mellow thick-thin difference and see-through c openings, which is the pair's real charm.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-noto-serif-tc: Noto Serif TC reads as a refined classic serif, its stems barely heavier than the arms joining them and its letters held open. And Baumans, which looks like glass tubing bent into letters, gives that traditional text a strikingly smooth heading to sit under.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-poly: Poly is a bookish serif whose bowls thin slightly at the sides and whose terminals pull back from the curve. Poly gives the page a gentle gradient of weight, while Baumans leads with a pen-like line that never changes.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-radley: Pipe-straight and bold, Baumans draws with the steadiness of a drawn string. Radley, a text serif with robust downstrokes and slender turns, brings authority and dignity, and that gives the pair its strongest quality.
